subject: Literacy
title: The sound /a/
objectives: Children will hear and say the sound /a/ at the start of words.
Children will find objects that start with /a/ with support.
content: Listening for the sound /a/ at the start of words, finding things that start with /a/, and the /a/ song.
teachingActivities: Say /a/ as a short, clear sound as in "ant", with no extra sound; show an open mouth; link the sound to an ant that wiggles; use real objects; children hear and say the sound only.
learnerActivities: Hear and say the sound /a/ at the start of words and find objects that start with /a/ with support.
resources: A toy ant or a picture of an ant
A toy axe or a picture
assessment: Observe whether each child says /a/ clearly and points to an object that starts with /a/.
expectedOutcomes: Points to an object that starts with /a/.

lessons.title: The ant says a, a, a
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will hear and say the sound /a/ as the ant sound.
successCriteria: Says the sound a when shown the ant
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say the sound /s/ and find objects that start with it.
resources: A toy ant or a picture of an ant
lessons.starter: Hold up the ant and say "This is an ant. The ant says a, a, a. Tickle, tickle, tickle." Wiggle your fingers.
teacherActivities: Say "a, a, a" in a short clear sound with your mouth open. Show how your mouth is open.
Say "a, a, a" together while the ant crawls on your arm.
Let each child look in the mirror and say a.
learnerActivities: Children watch your mouth and listen.
Children say "a" with you and wiggle their fingers.
Children copy a soft a and a loud a.
Child watches their mouth and says a.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "a, a, a" in a short clear sound with your mouth open. Show how your mouth is open. Children: Children watch your mouth and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "a, a, a" together while the ant crawls on your arm. Children: Children say "a" with you and wiggle their fingers.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "a" softly and loudly. Children: Children copy a soft a and a loud a.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child look in the mirror and say a. Children: Child watches their mouth and says a.

practical.title: Ant sound
steps: Give each child a pretend ant with their fingers.
Crawl the ant up your arm and say a, a, a.
practical.safety: Tell children the ant is a toy. Keep the sound gentle and watch that no one touches a real ant.

differentiation.support: Crawl the ant on the child’s arm and say a together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend what the ant says.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you make the ant sound?

lessons.conclusion: Put the ant to bed with a quiet a.
lessons.homeConnection: Crawl fingers up your child’s arm and say a, a, a.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hear and say the sound /a/ as the ant sound" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Ant, apple and axe
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will hear that ant, apple and axe start with the sound /a/.
successCriteria: Repeats the word and the first sound
Points to an object that starts with /a/
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say the sound /s/ and find objects that start with it.
resources: A toy ant, a toy apple, a picture of an axe
lessons.starter: Hold up the apple and say "Apple. A-pple. It starts with a." Show the ant and say "Ant. A-nt."
teacherActivities: Say each word slowly and stress the first sound: a-nt, a-pple, a-xe.
Put the three things on a tray and say "These all start with a."
Add a ball and ask "Does ball start with a?"
Let each child pick an a-object and say the word.
learnerActivities: Children repeat the word and the first sound.
Children touch each and say a.
Child shakes head or says no.
Child picks and says the word and a.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say each word slowly and stress the first sound: a-nt, a-pple, a-xe. Children: Children repeat the word and the first sound.
Step 2. Teacher: Put the three things on a tray and say "These all start with a." Children: Children touch each and say a.
Step 3. Teacher: Add a ball and ask "Does ball start with a?" Children: Child shakes head or says no.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child pick an a-object and say the word. Children: Child picks and says the word and a.

practical.title: A tray
steps: Put the ant, apple, axe picture and a ball on a tray.
Ask each child to take something that starts with a.
Say the word and the sound.
practical.safety: Use a toy apple and a picture for the axe. Never use a real axe. Keep objects clean and supervise handling.

differentiation.support: Offer two things, one that starts with a, and say the sound first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find another thing that starts with a.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What sound does apple start with?

expectedOutcomes: Hears /a/ at the start of words
Picks objects that start with /a/ with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects in the bag and say a.
lessons.homeConnection: Look for things that start with a, such as an apple, and say the sound.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "hear that ant, apple and axe start with the sound /a/" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: The a song
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will sing a song about the sound /a/ with actions.
successCriteria: Sings or hums the a song
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say the sound /s/ and find objects that start with it.
lessons.starter: Crawl the ant up your arm and sing "a, a, a". Ask "Who knows the ant song?"
teacherActivities: Sing the song slowly: "A, a, a, ant and apple and axe. A, a, a, what can you pack?" Show the cards.
Sing again and do the ant action.
Sing again and let children hold up a card at the right word.
Let a child lead the song with the ant.
learnerActivities: Children listen and look at the cards.
Children do the ant action and say a.
Child holds up the ant, apple or axe card.
Child leads and friends sing.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing the song slowly: "A, a, a, ant and apple and axe. A, a, a, what can you pack?" Show the cards. Children: Children listen and look at the cards.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing again and do the ant action. Children: Children do the ant action and say a.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing again and let children hold up a card at the right word. Children: Child holds up the ant, apple or axe card.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child lead the song with the ant. Children: Child leads and friends sing.

practical.title: Ant parade
steps: Give each child a card from the song.
Sing the song and parade round the mat.
Hold up the card at the right word.
practical.safety: Clear the floor so children can walk freely. Keep the volume gentle and use soft cards.

differentiation.support: Sing softly with the child and do the actions together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sing the song to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Sings the a song with actions
lessons.conclusion: Sing a quiet last verse and put the ant to bed.
lessons.homeConnection: Sing the ant song at home with finger actions.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sing a song about the sound /a/ with actions" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Find the a things
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will find objects that start with /a/ in a sound hunt.
successCriteria: Says the word and the sound
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say the sound /s/ and find objects that start with it.
resources: Six objects, three starting with /a/ and three that do not
lessons.starter: Say "Let us hunt for a things. A, a, a." Show the empty basket.
teacherActivities: Hide the objects around the room in easy places.
Say "Find an a thing" and let each child look.
Ask "Does it start with a?" and say the word.
Put the a things in the basket and the others on the mat.
learnerActivities: Children watch where you put the objects.
Child finds an object and brings it back.
Child says yes or no and the word.
Child sorts the objects.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hide the objects around the room in easy places. Children: Children watch where you put the objects.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Find an a thing" and let each child look. Children: Child finds an object and brings it back.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Does it start with a?" and say the word. Children: Child says yes or no and the word.
Step 4. Teacher: Put the a things in the basket and the others on the mat. Children: Child sorts the objects.

practical.title: A hunt
steps: Hide six objects in easy places in the room.
Children find objects and bring them to the mat.
Sort the a objects into the basket.
practical.safety: Hide objects only in clear, low places away from hazards. Supervise the search and keep children together.

differentiation.support: Walk with the child and point to the object after saying the sound.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to hide an a-object for a friend to find.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Finds objects starting with /a/ with support
lessons.conclusion: Count the objects in the basket and say a.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a sound hunt at home for things that start with a.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "find objects that start with /a/ in a sound hunt" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

lessons.title: Week 2 a check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child hears and says /a/.
successCriteria: Points to an object that starts with /a/
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can hear and say the sound /s/ and find objects that start with it.
lessons.starter: Crawl the ant and say "a". Show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: ant sound, a-objects and the song.
At each station ask "What sound?" and "Which one starts with a?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child says a and points.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: ant sound, a-objects and the song. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What sound?" and "Which one starts with a?" Children: Child says a and points.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Sound stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use large, clean objects.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to name two more a words.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says /a/ clearly; points to an object starting with /a/; joins in the song.

questions.question: What sound does the ant make?
Show me something that starts with a.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the ant with a soft a.
lessons.homeConnection: Play sound games at home with the sound a.
